tell: A thrombopoietin receptor agonist whose exposure falls by about 59% when taken with a high-calcium meal.

clues.text: Oral absorption is at least 52%, and a high-fat, high-calcium breakfast cuts exposure by about 59%. Over 99% is bound to plasma proteins, and feces carry 59% of the dose.
The free acid has a molecular weight of 442.5, and the olamine salt is practically insoluble in aqueous buffer.
Approved under NDA 022291 as tablets from 12.5 to 100 mg, plus a powder for oral suspension, dosed once daily.
Boxed warning for severe hepatotoxicity and hepatic decompensation. No contraindications are listed; anemia and nausea are among the most common reactions.
Thrombocytopenia in patients 1 year and older with persistent or chronic immune thrombocytopenia, and in hepatitis C patients to allow interferon-based therapy.
A thrombopoietin receptor agonist that binds the transmembrane domain of the TPO receptor, driving megakaryocyte proliferation and platelet production.
The generic name begins with E and has eleven letters.
